title: Playing from memory, Tipperary again, and Sousa marches
summary: He played melodies from memory while others faked, and praised Sousa's marches; he heard Sousa's band as a boy.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: when you played those dances did they ever play any pieces without music at all that you would just know from memory and the other fellows would fake if somebody would come up and request something like temporary and you didn't have the music for it would you still play the piece for them yeah sure would they put in variations see I'd play a piece two or three times by note

I wouldn't need no I wouldn't need no notes to play it because I could play it just as good as ever yeah just like I tell you the first time I played the Irish child this fella must have been a a few of the Irish and he'd come up after he played Tipperary once and I believe we played two pieces and they'd come up there and say he says I wish you'd play Tipperary over again he said if you'll do it he said I'll treat the whole gang I said you don't have to do that I said if you want us to play Tipperary
